import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology
open Set MeasureTheory
namespace BasisObjects
abbrev Rn (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
noncomputable def content {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (r : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i)
    (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ r),
      ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
def euclideanLift (n : ℕ) : Rn n × ℝ → WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2
end BasisObjects

namespace IntervalProduct
abbrev Rn := BasisObjects.Rn
def I : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
def F (n : ℕ) (E : Set (Rn n)) : Set (Rn n × ℝ) := E ×ˢ I
def j (n : ℕ) (p : WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ)) : Rn (n + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => p.fst i) p.snd)
def unj (n : ℕ) (v : Rn (n + 1)) : WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin n => v i.castSucc), v (Fin.last n))
def G (n : ℕ) (E : Set (Rn n)) : Set (Rn (n + 1)) :=
  j n '' (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n '' F n E)
noncomputable def H {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  letI : MeasurableSpace X := borel X
  letI : BorelSpace X := ⟨rfl⟩
  MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a A
noncomputable def cost {ι X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (U : ι → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ a
noncomputable def realCost {ι X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (U : ι → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, (ENNReal.ofReal (Metric.diam (U i))) ^ a
def Cover {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
def RealCover {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ (∀ i, Bornology.IsBounded (U i)) ∧ ∀ i, Metric.diam (U i) ≤ δ
end IntervalProduct
open IntervalProduct
value.representation: n is the original natural n₀, including zero; E remains a subset of BasisObjects.Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Ordinary X × ℝ uses Mathlib's maximum product metric. WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) uses the L² product metric: here 2 is the extended nonnegative real exponent, not the coordinate count. EuclideanSpace is PiLp 2 over Fin n. The explicit j appends the last real coordinate with Fin.snoc and unj truncates at castSucc and reads Fin.last; T009 proves this is a bijective isometry. G is exactly the set of coordinate concatenations of E and I, as an image under these explicit functions, in Euclidean Rn(n+1). E001 transports dimension from the maximum product to the L² product; no unproved metric identification is definitional. H fixes the canonical Borel measurable structure locally, avoiding any extra measurability premise on X or A. content is the exact frozen basis definition; powers are ENNReal real powers, infima/suprema and nonnegative sums remain in ℝ≥0∞ with ∞ allowed. cost retains the nonempty-member supremum; for positive exponents an empty member costs zero. RealCover explicitly includes boundedness before using real diameters, and realCost uses their nonnegative finite casts. Cover is the finite extended-diameter condition, equivalent to RealCover at positive real scales. N004 supplies finiteness before any use of NNReal representatives or toReal; standard cast order/addition compatibility does not add an assumption. No M premise ports or background-note premise ports are introduced. The pinned product metric instances require Fact (1 ≤ p): this is a proof that the Lp exponent lies in the metric range, and at p=2 it is supplied by the library, not an additional project hypothesis. The pinned Prod.dist_eq is max of the coordinate distances. Fin n indexes exactly the initial n coordinates; Fin.castSucc preserves their values in Fin(n+1), and Fin.last n is the appended coordinate. In cost and content, ^ a has real exponent a on ENNReal; in the squared-distance formulas ^ 2 is the ordinary natural square of a real distance.

value.explanation: Export full N003 by the lower-infimum bound of N001 applied to T004, even when there is no admissible cover. Take suprema over positive real scales at exponents s and s+1 to obtain the Hausdorff-measure inequality. Both inequalities are unconditional in finiteness and require no measurability of A or covering sets.

source_steps.text: By the lower-infimum bound in N001, F004 implies C^s_δ(A)≤C^(s+1)_δ(A×I), including if no admissible product cover exists. This holds at every δ>0. Taking suprema over positive scales and using N001 for both positive exponents s and s+1 gives H^s(A)≤H^(s+1)(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s and the scale. These are the complete scale and measure inequalities asserted in the output proposition.

For an emetric space W, B⊆W, real a and r∈ℝ≥0∞, content(a,r,B)= inf_{U:ℕ→Set W} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} Σ'_i sup_{h:U_i nonempty} ediam(U_i)^a. Infima and sums take values in ℝ≥0∞. A failed condition has empty infimum ∞; the supremum over a nonemptiness proof is zero for an empty member. This is exactly BasisObjects.content in basis-registry.json /lean_header.

For a metric space W, B⊆W, a>0 and δ>0, C^a_δ(B)=content(a,ENNReal.ofReal δ,B). The original real-diameter convention is the infimum of Σ_i diam(U_i)^a over countable covers of B with diam(U_i)≤δ, empty members contributing zero. The proof establishes compatibility of these two formulations.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of W

definitions.type: unnormalized Hausdorff measure evaluated on a set
definitions.definition: For a Borel emetric space W, B⊆W and real a, H^a(B)=MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a B. This is the metric outer-measure construction with gauge r↦r^a and no dimensional prefactor, taking values in ℝ≥0∞.

binders.type: emetric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an emetric space
definitions.definition: For an emetric space W and B⊆W, dimH(B)=sup{d∈ℝ≥0 : H^d(B)=∞}, interpreted in ℝ≥0∞, using the Borel structure of W. This is Hausdorff dimension and gives dimH(∅)=0. A finite dimension can be represented by its nonnegative real value; we explicitly establish finiteness before doing so.
I=[0,1], the closed unit interval in ℝ.
For a metric space W, MaxProd(W)=W×ℝ with distance max(dist(x,y),|t-u|) between (x,t) and (y,u). For real normed W this is its usual maximum product norm.

definitions.type: family of real normed spaces indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: L2Prod(m)=WithLp 2 (Rn(m)×ℝ), with the library L² product norm and its induced metric.
For every natural m, euclideanLift m=WithLp.toLp 2 on Rn(m)×ℝ; it is the identity on underlying pairs. This is exactly the definition in the frozen basis header.

definitions.type: family of coordinate concatenation maps L2Prod(m)→Rn(m+1)
definitions.definition: For each natural m, j(m)(p) is the (m+1)-tuple whose first m coordinates are those of p.fst and whose last coordinate is p.snd. This defines a total coordinate concatenation map.
F=E×I, regarded during the cover argument as a subset of MaxProd(Rn(n₀)).
D=dimH(E), with E in its original Euclidean Rn(n₀) metric.
T=dimH(F), using the maximum product metric.
G consists of coordinate concatenations (x_0,…,x_{n₀-1},t) with x∈E and t∈I. This is exactly E×[0,1] under the original target's specified identification with Euclidean ℝ^(n₀+1).

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the real line
definitions.definition: volume denotes Lebesgue measure on the Borel measurable space ℝ, with values in ℝ≥0∞.

definitions.type: set indicator with a zero outside branch
definitions.definition: For a set B⊆W and function f:W→ℝ≥0∞, indicator(B,f)(t)=f(t) for t∈B and 0 otherwise. We write 1_B(t)c for indicator(B,constant c)(t), including c=∞; this uses a zero branch outside B.

lintegral(μ,f)=∫⁻ t,f(t)∂μ is the supremum of the integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions below f, for a measure μ on a measurable space W and f:W→ℝ≥0∞. No finiteness of the value is implicit.

1: # Retained authors, immutable interfaces and proof repair
2: 
3: This protocol is generic. No domain, historical node ID or particular notation
4: activates a repair. Task names below describe responsibilities, not a new ID scheme.
5: 
6: ## Preprocessing author and independent reviewer
7: 
8: The controller verifies actual accepted NL0/A authority, then retains one author
9: through optional shared extraction and interface construction. A no-change decision
10: skips incremental review. A changed source gets actual producer/substitution review
11: by the separate retained preprocessing reviewer. Located failures return to that
12: same author; changed candidates return to that same reviewer. Operational faults
13: pause rather than masquerading as mathematical revision requests.
14: 
15: The reviewer next checks the complete typed contract and plan: every external E
16: and full P including all hypotheses, quantifiers and domains; relevant definitions,
17: structure fields, library parameter/index meanings, coercions and nonvacuity. Read
18: the actual pinned definitions instead of guessing from notation. A well-typed
19: encoding may still strengthen or weaken the source. The reviewer is independent
20: of the author, while retaining its own earlier findings; disclose both facts.
21: 
22: Only a complete actual passing semantic receipt opens freeze and proof dispatch.
23: Freeze source, pins, complete endpoint types and the meaning-determining header.
24: Save the handoff and close both preprocessing roles. An unchanged rejected proposal
25: does not justify repeated reviews. This semantic authority is inherited at final
26: machine acceptance only when the actual final artifact still matches it.
27: 
28: ## Local proof work
29: 
30: Each node has its own retained author. Ordinary compiler/API/tactic feedback stays
31: with that author. A 180-second native timeout or heartbeat failure retains the
32: candidate and supplies frozen ST020 advice in the failed tool result. Isolate the
33: expensive application, repair and recheck the unchanged target. There is no total
34: case, token, call, repair-round or turn allowance by default.
35: 
36: `report_proof_obstruction` requests a diagnosis; it does not itself finish the
37: node. The original author waits for this tool result, releases its active model
38: slot, and retains its native conversation, checked helpers and drafts. A separate
39: evidence-informed diagnostic uses the same bounded proof lane and an immutable
40: snapshot of this node's source, interface and selected actual attempts. It does
41: not wait for other nodes to complete or inspect their proof bodies.
42: 
43: Ordinary proof errors remain local. A failed compile or resource limit does not
44: establish a source defect. LOCAL_PROOF_REPAIR and UNRESOLVED return concrete
45: feedback to the same author, which continues without an attempt/idle threshold.
46: Rewording the same evidence reuses the stored diagnostic rather than sampling a
47: new verdict. Healthy siblings are neither cancelled nor restarted.
48: 
49: A source allegation must quote the current source, state its permitted
50: hypotheses and claimed conclusion, locate a false implication or important
51: missing mathematical justification, and explain why it is not merely a Lean
52: implementation difficulty. Only a qualified diagnostic confirming such evidence
53: can request the source-review boundary. Distinguish an incomplete source argument
54: from a false theorem. Report the specific issue once; retain all unsuccessful
55: attempts and diagnostic costs.
56: 
57: The diagnostic cannot add premises or change frozen E/P and their meaning.
58: Only a located, compared and qualified interface defect can hand the node to the
59: existing interface-repair path. No fixed count of failed checks or idle replies
60: retires an author. Progress counters measure activity, not proof completion.
61: 
62: `INTERNAL_INTERFACE_REPAIR` returns a located T-statement/allowed-input defect to
63: the preprocessing author and separate reviewer after current-round handoffs.
64: Only steps may change: retain the entire public header, original H/E/P, source,
65: pins, output map and public representations. Preserve the old frozen revision.
66: Strict declaration/source-boundary checks precede an independent delta review
67: of changed steps and affected consumers. Exact unchanged scopes inherit the
68: bound parent receipt; a new actual receipt binds the new revision and review
69: scope. Rejected candidates/findings stay with the same repair roles. Close the
70: preprocessing roles at the existing successful freeze boundary. A closed role
71: is restored from its own saved handoff in a disclosed fresh carrier; no vanished
72: native conversation is claimed. Previously checked own bodies are candidates
73: until current native checks accept them; changed packets cannot inherit old
74: helper-check status. No sibling is forcibly closed for an obstruction.
75: If a reviewed revision removes an old node, its retained repair handoff closes
76: only at final workflow acceptance. Preserve that old obstruction rather than
77: relabeling it as a successful local proof.
78: 
79: A located protected public-contract defect or confirmed substantial source gap
80: pauses with saved evidence for the user. Uncertain difficulty stays with the author. No automatic unfreeze, source rewrite,
81: whole-workflow restart or new model/profile is authorized. Repeated identical
82: obligation/evidence after a located advice handoff stays an explicit checkpoint;
83: it is not a reason to resample a diagnostic or declare mathematical impossibility.
84: 
85: ## Assembly and final machine acceptance
86: 
87: Attempt mechanical assembly first. If it fails with an actual connection error,
88: use the connection author under the immutable contract. Recheck the complete
89: standalone file, all internal producer dependencies and actual kernel trust.
90: No `sorry`, undeclared project premise or unproved substitute may remain.
91: 
92: Normal final Audit B checks actual full E/P types by native definitional equality,
93: exact frozen header/pins and bound semantic authority, plus complete proof closure.
94: It calls no final semantic model. Its receipt says `FROZEN_INTERFACE_SEMANTICS_INHERITED`,
95: not that a new independent final review took place. Source qualifications remain.
96: 
97: Only a valid proof with genuine endpoint/meaning drift may open B-final. Missing
98: compilation, changed provenance, missing dependencies or `sorry` cannot use this
99: exception. Actual B-final fidelity PASS permits warning-qualified delivery and
100: records the freeze-integrity defect. A nonpass pauses locally and asks the user:
101: 
102: - `deliver-actual`: deliver the compiled statement and findings, explicitly **not**
103:   completion of the original target.
104: - `recheck`: perform the explicitly requested new detailed semantic review, keeping
105:   earlier findings, costs and its actual review scope in the evidence.
106: - `reset-translation`: release translation processes, remove translation-generated
107:   source/native/temp files, retain original NL0/A and cost ledgers, and rerun only
108:   translation. Report the freeze defect to developers.
109: 
110: These are exact-incident `yui.py final-decision` controls displayed in the offline
111: pause report. None is automatic. A stale incident, changed owner, changed artifact
112: or unconfirmed owned-process cleanup blocks the action. User cancellation remains
113: available. A user acceptance of files never grants fidelity or original-goal PASS.
114: 
115: ## Evidence and lifetimes
116: 
117: A submission is a durable handoff, followed by a confirmed native turn interrupt;
118: its role waits without another provider request. The native thread is reused for
119: that role's next assignment. Only the specified accepted handoff closes a role;
120: a fault preserves the carrier, drafts and diagnostics. Controller-authenticated
121: restoration of an interrupted dynamic-tool result is logged and hash-bound; unknown
122: calls or altered history remain rejected.
123: 
124: Reuse only exact checked contexts. Successful bodies copied between retained proof
125: runs are candidates until current Lean checks accept them. Save rejected drafts,
126: actual retries/waits and all reported usage. Selected proof rounds use bound
127: `proof-selection.json`; retained earlier failures are not free or new successes.
128: Missing usage or actual service tier remains unknown; cached/reasoning tokens are
129: subsets. Owner monitoring is bounded read-only observation and supplies no hints.

import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology
open Set MeasureTheory
namespace BasisObjects
abbrev Rn (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
noncomputable def content {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (r : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i)
    (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ r),
      ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
def euclideanLift (n : ℕ) : Rn n × ℝ → WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2
end BasisObjects

namespace IntervalProduct
abbrev Rn := BasisObjects.Rn
def I : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
def F (n : ℕ) (E : Set (Rn n)) : Set (Rn n × ℝ) := E ×ˢ I
def j (n : ℕ) (p : WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ)) : Rn (n + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => p.fst i) p.snd)
def unj (n : ℕ) (v : Rn (n + 1)) : WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin n => v i.castSucc), v (Fin.last n))
def G (n : ℕ) (E : Set (Rn n)) : Set (Rn (n + 1)) :=
  j n '' (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n '' F n E)
noncomputable def H {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  letI : MeasurableSpace X := borel X
  letI : BorelSpace X := ⟨rfl⟩
  MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a A
noncomputable def cost {ι X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (U : ι → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ a
noncomputable def realCost {ι X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (U : ι → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, (ENNReal.ofReal (Metric.diam (U i))) ^ a
def Cover {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
def RealCover {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ (∀ i, Bornology.IsBounded (U i)) ∧ ∀ i, Metric.diam (U i) ≤ δ
end IntervalProduct
open IntervalProduct

value.text: Fix X,A,a and assume L1: a>0. Work with X's Borel structure, so M001 applies and gives H^a(A)=sup_{r>0} content(a,r,A) over extended nonnegative r. For arbitrary δ, temporarily assume L2: δ>0. At the finite scale ofReal δ, every admissible covering member has finite extended diameter, hence is bounded and has ediam equal to its real diameter cast to ℝ≥0∞. The nonemptiness-proof supremum in D004 is the displayed diameter power on a nonempty member and is zero on an empty member. For a>0 this agrees with assigning the empty member diameter zero and 0^a=0. Thus the nested infima are exactly the original admissible-cover infimum, with no prefactor. A finite family can be padded by empty sets. For an arbitrary countable index type choose an injection into ℕ; at each image index put the unique original member and elsewhere put ∅. This preserves the union and all nonnegative sums. Conversely an ℕ-family is countable. Discharge L2 after this finite-scale interpretation, retaining its δ>0 antecedent for every δ. For arbitrary δ₁,δ₂, temporarily assume L3: 0<δ₁≤δ₂. Every δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover, so C^a_δ₂(A)≤C^a_δ₁(A). Discharge L3 and quantify the two scales. Every cost bounds its infimum above; a lower bound on every admissible cost bounds the infimum below. If the admissible family is empty its infimum is ∞, and the latter assertion remains true. For any positive extended scale r, if it is finite it is the cast of a positive real scale. The content at r=∞ is at most that at any fixed finite positive scale, since every finite-scale cover is also an ∞-cover. Hence the ∞ scale adds nothing to the supremum. We have proved H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0}C^a_δ(A), and each such content is ≤H^a(A).

For the arbitrary δ,ε, temporarily assume L4: δ>0 and ε>0. Suppose L5: C^a_δ(A)=0. if every admissible cost were ≥ε, the lower-bound property in F001 would imply C^a_δ(A)≥ε>0, a contradiction. Thus an admissible cover of cost <ε exists. Discharge L5 to obtain the forward implication. In terms of the nested infima in D004, any failed cover or diameter condition has value ∞ and cannot give a value <ε, so the approximation provides an actual admissible family. Conversely assume L6: for every positive tolerance there exists an admissible cover of smaller cost. This forces the nonnegative content to be zero: a positive value, finite or infinite, has some positive finite real below it, contradicting the upper bound by those costs. Discharge L6, then L4, and quantify the arbitrary positive scale and tolerance. This proves the zero-content approximation equivalence for every positive scale. These arguments also cover an empty admissible family, whose content is ∞.

By F001, H^a(A)=0 implies each positive-scale content is zero; F002 then gives the required arbitrarily small covers at every scale. Conversely, those covers make every positive-scale content zero by F002, and their supremum is zero by F001. This proves the full equivalence and all asserted content properties. Discharge L1 to retain a>0 as an antecedent and universally quantify X,A,a and the scale/tolerance variables. No boundedness or measurability assumption on A is used.

Fix X,A,q and assume L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix arbitrary real δ,ε and assume L2: δ>0 and ε>0. Put r=min(1,δ), so 0<r≤1 and r≤δ. By N001 with exponent q, scale r and tolerance ε/4 there exists a countable r-cover U of A whose total q-cost is <ε/4; reindex it as a sequence with empty padding if necessary. In particular its members have finite diameter.

Choose U from F001 and put d_i=diam(U_i), with d_i=0 on empty members. For each natural i define a_seq(i)=min(r,(ε·2^(-i-3))^(1/q)). Both entries of this minimum are positive, so 0<a_seq(i)≤r and a_seq(i)^q≤ε·2^(-i-3). The nonnegative geometric series has sum Σ_{i≥0}2^(-i-3)=1/4 (its partial sums are (1/4)(1-2^(-m)) for the first m terms). Hence Σ a_seq(i)^q≤ε/4. Put r_i=max(d_i,a_seq(i)). Then 0<r_i≤r≤1 and r_i^q=max(d_i^q,a_seq(i)^q)≤d_i^q+a_seq(i)^q. Summing nonnegative terms, using F001 and the geometric bound, gives Σ r_i^q<ε/2. Numerical padding changes no covering set and works even if X is a singleton.

For each natural i put N_i=ceil(1/r_i), a positive integer. Then 1/N_i≤r_i and N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i, since 0<r_i≤1. The closed intervals [h/N_i,(h+1)/N_i], 0≤h<N_i, cover I. Define W_seq(i,h)=U_i×[h/N_i,(h+1)/N_i]. In the maximum product metric any two points of this product have distance at most r_i, since the first-coordinate diameter is d_i≤r_i and the second-coordinate interval length is 1/N_i≤r_i. The product family covers A×I, and its index set {(i,h):i∈ℕ,0≤h<N_i} is countable. Empty products have zero cost. By N001 this countable family may be reindexed into ℕ without changing the union or sum. It is a δ-cover, and its total (q+1)-cost is at most Σ_i N_i r_i^(q+1)≤2Σ_i r_i^q<ε. The power cancellation r_i^(q+1)/r_i=r_i^q is valid because r_i>0. Rearranging these nonnegative sums is legitimate, and the upper bound is finite.

F003 holds for arbitrary positive δ,ε. Discharge L2 to obtain existence of the stated arbitrarily fine arbitrarily cheap covers. Since q+1>0, N001, now for MaxProd(X), A×I and exponent q+1, implies H^(q+1)(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves the output proposition on the whole asserted domain without any positive-diameter assumption on the covering sets.

Fix X,A,s,δ and assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Set c=C^s_δ(A), possibly ∞. Take any sequence V and assume L2: V is a δ-cover of A×I in MaxProd(X). Put ρ_i=diam(V_i), A_i=π_X(V_i), B_i=π_ℝ(V_i). Every V_i is bounded, since its extended diameter is ≤δ<∞. Each projection has pairwise distances at most ρ_i, whence diam A_i≤ρ_i and diam B_i≤ρ_i≤δ. For a nonempty V_i, B_i is nonempty and bounded above and below: choose any one of its points and use the finite diameter bound. Thus inf B_i and sup B_i exist as real numbers. Put J_i=[inf B_i,sup B_i]. The least-upper-bound and greatest-lower-bound properties give B_i⊆J_i and sup B_i-inf B_i≤ρ_i: for every b,b'∈B_i one has b-b'≤ρ_i, and taking supremum in b then infimum in b' preserves the inequality. In particular inf B_i≤sup B_i. For empty V_i put ρ_i=0 and A_i=B_i=J_i=∅. Each J_i is a closed real interval or ∅, hence Borel measurable, and all projection bounds remain valid. This construction imposes no measurability on V_i or its projections.

For each nonempty member, apply M009 with endpoints inf B_i and sup B_i. By F001, volume(J_i)=ofReal(sup B_i-inf B_i)≤ρ_i. For an empty member volume(J_i)=volume(∅)=0=ρ_i by the empty-set axiom of a measure. Also I=[0,1] is closed and measurable and M009 with endpoints 0,1 gives volume(I)=1. Since I∩J_i⊆J_i, measure monotonicity gives volume(I∩J_i)≤volume(J_i)≤ρ_i; each intersection is measurable as an intersection of closed measurable sets.

Define g(t)=1_I(t)c and f_seq(i)(t)=1_{I∩J_i}(t)ρ_i^s. Fix any real t. Universal introduction in t gives g≤Σ_i f_seq(i) pointwise on ℝ, also if c=∞. F002 shows that every indicator summand is Borel measurable: its only values are a nonnegative constant and zero on complementary measurable pieces, hence it is also volume-almost-everywhere measurable. No product of an undefined infinite real quantity is used.

Integrate F003 over ℝ with Lebesgue measure. M011 gives lintegral(volume,g)≤lintegral(volume,Σ_i f_seq(i)). M012 for I and constant c, together with volume(I)=1 from F002, gives lintegral(volume,g)=c·1=c, even when c=∞.
